editorial_source: Mommers, M.J.C. & Caesar, F. (Veilig Leren Lezen / VLL kern methodology, Zwijsen) — the canonical Dutch K-1 phonics chunk inventory. The chunks themselves (digraphs, long-vowel doublings, diphthongs) are facts of Dutch orthography and not copyrightable; only the textbook presentation is. Academic fallback: de Graaff, S. & Bosman, A.M.T. (2012). Klanken en hun letters in Nederlandse woorden. Tijdschrift voor Orthopedagogiek 51, 67-83. SLO Tussendoelen Beginnende Geletterdheid also references this inventory.
policy_note: Dutch open vs closed syllable distinction is central: kaas (open, long vowel by spelling aa) vs kat (closed, short vowel). VLL kern 1-6 covers single letters + aa/ee/oo/uu doubling + sch/ch/ng/nk; kern 7-12 covers diphthongs + the ij/ei pair.
